text: The Race: which part of a car is this?

bank.q: Holds the cogs that let you go from first gear to fifth
The left-hand pedal you press to change gear
Carries burnt gases away from the engine and out at the back
Keeps the engine cool by passing hot water through thin fins at the front
Driven by the engine, it charges the battery while you drive
Makes the tiny flash that lights the petrol in each cylinder
Pull it out and wipe it to check the oil level
A lever you pull up to stop the parked car rolling away
Cleans up the exhaust fumes, and is often stolen for its precious metals
A rubber loop that drives the alternator; a pair of tights can stand in for it in an emergency
The lid over the engine at the front; Americans call it the hood
Where the luggage goes; Americans call it the trunk
The dial that shows how fast you're going
The dial showing how fast the engine is turning, in thousands per minute
Sticks out from the side so you can see what's behind and beside you
A shiny cover over the middle of the wheel, easily lost on a kerb
Sweeps the rain off the glass in front of you
Bursts out of the steering wheel in a crash
Part of the suspension that stops the car bouncing after a bump
Blinks orange to show which way you're turning

text: The Race: what's this internet word?

bank.q: Junk email you never asked for, named after a tinned meat
A fake email pretending to be your bank, fishing for your password
A small file a website leaves on your computer to remember you
A barrier that blocks unwanted traffic from reaching your computer
The program you look at websites with, like Chrome or Safari
Any software written to damage or spy on your computer
The # symbol used to tag a topic on social media
A little picture like a smiley face or a thumbs-up, sent in a message
A funny picture or idea copied and passed around online, often with new captions
Someone who posts nasty things just to start arguments
The little picture or character that stands for you online
A test of wobbly letters or traffic lights to prove you're not a robot
An audio show you download or stream, often a chat about one topic
An online diary of written posts
A photo you take of yourself, often at arm's length
Someone who uses a fake identity online to trick people into a relationship
A tempting headline written just to make you click: 'You won't believe what happened next'
Someone paid by brands to show products to their many followers
What a video has 'gone' when millions share it within days
Suddenly cutting off all contact with someone, without a word
